newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed on Friday in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said.

"Government securities were narrowly mixed amid continued uncertainty over market direction. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher but bond prices were slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.18/2.13 percent compared with Thursday's yield of 2.03/1.98 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.15/2.10 percent against 1.93/1.88 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$99.20/99.25 from Thursday's close of S$99.45/99.50, September 2001 at S$96.50/96.60 versus S$96.60/96.70 and June 2003 at S$94.47/94.52 against S$94.70/94.75.
The interbank rate was unchanged from Thursday's 3-5/8 3-1/2 percent.
